name: Ethical Marketing Presentations
description: Two presentation tasks exploring ethical marketing from different perspectives
author: IELTS Practice Team

questions.title: Ethical Marketing: Problems and Solutions – An Academic Review
questions.prompt:
Your role: You are a university student researching ethical marketing. You are giving a presentation to your class and your teacher.

Your audience: Your classmates and teacher. They expect you to be fair, honest, and objective.

Your task: Present a balanced review of ethical marketing. You must explain:

  1. What the main problems are with ethical marketing today, such as greenwashing and misleading claims.
  2. What solutions companies like Threadline are trying.
  3. Whether you think these solutions are working.

What to include:

  • At least three reporting verbs from the lesson, such as suggests, indicates, notes, demonstrates, argues.
  • At least three examples of hedging language, such as may, might, appears to, seems to, perhaps, a degree of.
  • Evidence or examples to support your points.
  • A balanced conclusion. Do not simply say that "Threadline is perfect" or that "ethical marketing is dead."

questions.title: Threadline: Leading the Way in Ethical Marketing
questions.prompt:
Your role: You are the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of Threadline. You are giving a presentation to potential customers and business investors.

Your audience: People who care about the environment and want to support responsible brands. You want to inspire and convince them.

Your task: Give a persuasive presentation explaining why Threadline has genuinely solved many of the problems associated with ethical marketing. You must explain:

  1. Why traditional marketing practices were problematic.
  2. What Threadline is doing differently, including its reselling platform, transparency, and commitment to inclusivity.
  3. Why your audience should support Threadline.

What to include:

  • At least three examples of strong, emotional language, such as clearly, genuinely, always, must, proves, demonstrates.
  • At least one powerful call to action, such as "We must act now..." or "Join us in...".
  • A personal story or vivid example to make your message memorable.
  • A confident and inspiring closing statement.
